patients.summary: Retired accountant who joins the practice at 70 with hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, a remote stroke and alcohol use disorder in early remission. Over the next decade he develops presbycusis, aortic stenosis, multi-infarct dementia, locally advanced prostate cancer on androgen deprivation, a Zenker diverticulum, central cord syndrome after a fall, and in June 2026 an acute subdural hematoma that is evacuated. Outside records are patchy; his daughter carries much of the communication.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

70-year-old retired accountant transferring care; wanted a practice where he could reach the doctor directly. Lives alone in Easthampton. Prior primary care elsewhere for years; records release signed today.

HISTORY
- Hypertension since roughly 2005, on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Home cuff readings he recalls in the 130s.
- Type 2 diabetes since about 2009, metformin 500 mg twice daily. Last A1c he remembers was 'under 7'. No hypoglycemia. No foot sores.
- High cholesterol, atorvastatin 20 mg at night, no muscle complaints.
- Neck: long-standing stiffness, told years ago it was arthritis of the neck (cervical spondylosis). No arm numbness or weakness. Uses heat, nothing else.
- Hay fever in spring and late summer, loratadine when needed.
- Stroke around 2011. Vague on details: was in the hospital a couple of days, 'it all came back' within weeks. No deficits he is aware of.
- Alcohol: describes years of heavy drinking that he calls a problem; stopped completely in late November and has not had a drink since. Going to meetings. Wants it on his record so we can help him stay on track.

SURGICAL: none.
ALLERGIES: none to medications.
FAMILY: father had coronary disease and a narrowed aortic valve; mother had Alzheimer disease late in life; older brother treated for prostate cancer.
SOCIAL: never used tobacco. No other substances. Retired from accounting. Drives. Has a daughter who lives nearby.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, bowel or urinary trouble, weight change, mood complaints.

EXAM
Vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing, pleasant, a bit hard of hearing when I turned away.
HEENT: canals clear, oropharynx normal. Neck: supple, reduced rotation both directions, no bruits, no thyromegaly.
Heart: regular rate and rhythm. Lungs: clear throughout.
Abdomen: soft, nontender. Ext: no edema; feet intact skin, monofilament sensation normal, pulses 2+.
Neuro: alert and oriented, fluent, strength 5/5 throughout, gait steady.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Hypertension: near goal on HCTZ. Continue; recheck with BMP.
2. Type 2 diabetes: metformin continued. A1c, urine microalbumin today. Eye exam with his optometrist yearly.
3. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 20 continued. Lipids today.
4. Remote stroke, recovered: on statin. Will review old records when they come.
5. Alcohol use disorder, early remission: encouraged, meetings, he knows he can call. AUDIT-C 0 for the past weeks.
6. Cervical spondylosis, allergic rhinitis: stable.
7. Health maintenance: hepatitis C screen today. Colonoscopy and vaccines per old records. Wellness visit in spring.

Return in about 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mr. Fleming,

Your blood work from the 10th is back. Kidney function, potassium, blood counts and thyroid are normal. A1c is right around 7, which is reasonable for you. LDL cholesterol is under 100 on the atorvastatin. Urine protein is normal and the hepatitis C screen is negative.

No changes. See you in the spring for your wellness visit.

Your primary care physician

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior primary care office (64 pages). Scanned to media. Abstracted:

- Colonoscopy 2012: normal to the cecum, no polyps. No repeat advised given age.
- Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine 10/2011. Tdap 4/2014. Yearly flu shots there.
- 2011 hospital discharge summary: minor ischemic stroke, symptoms resolved before discharge; discharged on his usual medications.
- Medication list matches ours: HCTZ 25, metformin 500 twice daily, atorvastatin 20, loratadine as needed.
- No drug allergies listed.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Prior records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Old stroke well recovered by their summary. Vaccines entered. Colonoscopy 2012 normal; no further screening at his age unless symptoms.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
INITIAL WELLNESS VISIT

Health risk questionnaire reviewed with him. Still abstinent, about six months now, attending meetings twice weekly. Walks most days. Eats out a lot since living alone.

Function: handles his own finances (still does a few friends' taxes), shopping, cooking, driving. No falls this year. Hearing: says people mumble; not ready to do anything about it. Vision: readers, sees optometrist.
Mood: PHQ-2 negative.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 3 words recalled, clock normal.
Home safety reviewed. Advance directive: none; information given, he will think about naming his daughter.

Exam brief: vitals per flowsheet, heart regular, lungs clear, feet normal sensation.

Plan:
- PCV13 today; he had the polysaccharide vaccine in 2011, so pneumococcal series complete after this.
- Shingles vaccine: new two-dose vaccine expected; will offer when we have it.
- Diabetes follow-up in July with labs.
- Personalized prevention plan printed for him.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for sugar and pressure check. Taking everything. Allergies acting up with the hay season, loratadine helps. Eight months without a drink. Neck stiff in the mornings as usual.
O: Vitals reviewed. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet: skin intact, sensation normal.
A/P: Diabetes and hypertension, both doing fine on current regimen. A1c and BMP today. No changes. Optometry letter requested. Back in January.

documents.title: A1c and BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs stable, A1c in range, electrolytes and kidney function normal. Letter to patient.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Re: George Fleming

Seen for his annual diabetic eye examination. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy in either eye, maculae flat. Mild nuclear lens changes both eyes, not visually significant. Updated reading prescription. Return in one year.

Optometry

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Screening questions negative. VIS given. Tolerated, waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting 90-day supplies of metformin 500 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg and HCTZ 25 mg; his plan prefers mail-order quantities. Pended for PCP.

documents.title: Refills approved
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Approved 90 days with 3 refills each. Labs current.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes / HTN visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One year with us. Doing well. Sober more than a year now, proud of it. Shoveling snow without trouble. No hypoglycemia, no numbness in the feet, no chest symptoms.

Exam: BP and weight per flowsheet. Neck with limited rotation, unchanged. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Monofilament intact both feet, pulses good.

Plan: yearly labs today (A1c, CMP, lipids, urine albumin). Continue HCTZ, metformin, atorvastatin. Shingles vaccine now in stock; RN visit to start the series.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi George, everything from your yearly labs looks good: A1c steady, kidneys and liver normal, cholesterol at goal, no protein in the urine. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. I will call about the shingles shots.

documents.title: Shingrix #1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Counseled that the arm may ache and he may feel tired for a day or two. Dose 2 due in 2 to 6 months; will give at his May wellness visit.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SUBSEQUENT WELLNESS VISIT

Interval: uneventful. First dose of shingles vaccine gave him a sore, heavy arm for a day.
Alcohol: abstinent since late 2016, still at meetings weekly.
Function: fully independent; drives, manages his money and medications. No falls.
Cognition: Mini-Cog normal (3/3, clock intact).
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Hearing: complains more in restaurants; offered a referral, he wants to wait.
Vision: optometrist yearly.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, feet with normal sensation.

Plan: Shingrix dose 2 today, series complete. Diabetes check in July. Updated prevention plan given.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, helping his daughter move furniture tomorrow, asked to push his check-up two weeks. Rebooked.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Feels well. Summer allergies managed with loratadine. Checks sugars occasionally, fasting 120s to 140s. Heart regular, lungs clear, feet fine. A1c and BMP today. Same medicines. Next visit after the holidays, with yearly labs.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c and BMP unremarkable. No action.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Annual dilated exam for George Fleming: no diabetic changes in either retina. Early lens opacities, stable from last year. Vision correctable to 20/25 each eye. See in 12 months.

Optometry

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine given IM right deltoid, lot and expiration in the immunization record. No prior reactions. Observed, left in good condition.

documents.title: Hearing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: hearing.

He is ready to have his hearing looked at. Over the last few years it has slowly gotten harder to follow conversation, worst at his meetings and in restaurants where there is background noise. Turns the TV up. No ear pain, drainage, ringing he notices, or spinning. Never worked around loud machinery; no gunfire. No new medications.

Exam: external canals clear, tympanic membranes normal both sides. Misses several whispered words on each side. Rest of exam not repeated today.

A/P:
1. Gradual bilateral hearing loss, likely age related. ENT/audiology referral placed.
2. Diabetes: A1c drawn today since he was due; yearly labs at the January visit.
